european-organic.label: Medieval organic (Europe)
european-organic.description: A medieval town grown by accretion: winding streets radiating from a market, narrow burgage plots under gabled timber houses, a parish church in each quarter.

bastide.label: Bastide (planned grid)
bastide.description: A planned town of the Middle Ages: a regular grid of rectangular blocks around an arcaded market square, a wall, and stone row houses with arcades.

medina.label: Medina (North Africa)
medina.description: A walled Maghrebi town: a dense maze of covered lanes and dead ends around the great mosque and the souk, flat-roofed courtyard houses of mud and plaster.

chinese.label: Chinese walled city
chinese.description: A walled city on a strict square grid with a drum tower at its centre; walled courtyard houses (siheyuan) under tiled hip roofs.

japanese-jokamachi.label: Japanese castle town (jōkamachi)
japanese-jokamachi.description: A castle town: the lord’s castle commands a web of organic streets, with samurai yashiki and merchant quarters packed below it, under tiled hip roofs.

indian-temple.label: Indian temple town
indian-temple.description: A temple town on a square grid: the temple precinct sits at the centre, with long rows of narrow brick houses around courtyards (mutram).

roman-core.label: Roman castrum core
roman-core.description: The core of a Roman colony: a castrum grid with a forum at the crossing of cardo and decumanus, a wall with gates, brick domus and insulae.

elven.label: Elven forest town
elven.description: A forest town of living wood: organic paths between tree houses and domed pavilions, a sacred grove at the centre, a hedge instead of a wall.

dwarven.label: Dwarven hold
dwarven.description: A mountain hold: terraced halls cut into rock behind a straight stone wall, flat roofs, rooms of massive stone.

necropolis.label: Necropolis (city of the dead)
necropolis.description: A city of the dead on a regular grid: mausoleums in hip-roofed stone, a wall, and a mortuary temple at the centre.

russian-kremlin.label: Russian kremlin and posad
russian-kremlin.description: A kremlin on its hill with the posad (trading quarter) around it: organic streets, a palisade and log izba houses under gabled roofs.

aztec.label: Aztec city (Tenochtitlan)
aztec.description: A ceremonial city on a square grid: a sacred precinct at the centre, flat-roofed adobe calli houses grouped in compounds.

inca.label: Inca city (Cusco)
inca.description: A stone city on terraces: trapezoidal compounds (kancha) laid out on a rectilinear plan around the ushnu platform, gabled stone houses.

byzantine-greek.label: Byzantine hill town (Mystras)
byzantine-greek.description: A hill town in terraces on the slope (Mystras): stepped streets, stone houses of one to three storeys under tiled roofs, an organic wall.

venetian-lagoon.label: Venetian lagoon town
venetian-lagoon.description: A lagoon town of tall brick houses (three to four storeys) on narrow plots, a market at its centre, no wall: the water is the defence.

persian.label: Persian city (Isfahan)
persian.description: A Persian city around a great maidan (square), with bazaar shops under brick domes and vaulted passages, protected by a wall.

ottoman.label: Ottoman town (Bursa)
ottoman.description: An Ottoman town: organic streets around the market (çarşı), dukkan shops and timber houses under tiled hip roofs, no town wall.

sahel.label: Sahelian mud town (Djenne)
sahel.description: A Sahelian mud town (Djenné): a great mud-brick mosque at its centre, flat-roofed Sudano-Sahelian houses of one or two storeys, irregular lanes.

hanseatic.label: Hanseatic port (Lubeck)
hanseatic.description: A Hanseatic port (Lübeck): a grid of streets bounded by a wall, tall brick gable houses of three to five storeys (Giebelhäuser) with deep merchant plots.

korean.label: Korean walled town (Hanyang)
korean.description: A walled Korean town (Hanyang): hanok houses of wood under tiled hip roofs, a market at the centre, organic streets within the wall.

wizard-city.label: Wizard city
wizard-city.description: A wizard city on a radial plan: a tower at the centre, a circular wall, stone houses of two to four storeys under hip roofs.

gnomish.label: Gnomish canal town
gnomish.description: A gnomish canal town: very tall narrow brick houses (five to seven storeys) under pyramidal roofs, a clock tower at the centre.

stilt-town.label: Stilt town (marsh folk)
stilt-town.description: A scattered village of marsh folk on stilts: round thatched houses standing over the water, no centre and no enclosure.

barbarian.label: Barbarian: Germanic village
barbarian.description: A Germanic village: byre-houses with thatched gabled roofs scattered in a circle of fields, no wall.

barbarian-celtic.label: Barbarian: Celtic ringfort
barbarian-celtic.description: A Celtic ringfort: round thatched wattle houses in concentric rings behind a palisade.

barbarian-norse.label: Barbarian: Norse farmstead cluster
barbarian-norse.description: A cluster of Norse farmsteads: turf-roofed longhouses scattered around a common area, no wall.

norse-ringfort.label: Norse ring fortress (Trelleborg)
norse-ringfort.description: A Norse ring fortress (Trelleborg): a circular palisade, radial streets and long timber houses with gabled roofs.

maya.label: Maya city (ceremonial core, sacbeob)
maya.description: A Maya city: a ceremonial core joined by causeways (sacbeob), thatched round wattle houses scattered in compounds around it.

khmer.label: Khmer city (Angkor)
khmer.description: A Khmer city (Angkor): rectangular blocks bounded by a moat, houses of wood on stilts under gabled roofs, no inner wall.

celtic-oppidum.label: Celtic oppidum
celtic-oppidum.description: A Celtic oppidum: an organic layout inside a long defensive wall, round thatched wattle houses.

orcish.label: Orcish war camp
orcish.description: An orcish war camp: huts of hide on a conical frame scattered in a circle, no order and no wall.

halfling.label: Halfling shire
halfling.description: A halfling shire: smials (houses dug into hillsides) under turf domes, scattered in a circle, with small gardens.

kraal.label: Kraal (African homestead)
kraal.description: An African kraal: beehive thatched huts arranged radially around a central cattle pen.

native-iroquoian.label: Native American: Iroquoian longhouse village
native-iroquoian.description: An Iroquoian longhouse village: bark longhouses with barrel roofs in rows along a line, inside an oval palisade.

native-pueblo.label: Native American: Pueblo
native-pueblo.description: A Pueblo: adobe rooms stacked in terraces up to five storeys, around an open plaza.

native-plains.label: Native American: Plains tipi camp
native-plains.description: A Plains tipi camp: hide tipis in a radial circle around a central open space; no walls.

nomad-camp.label: Nomad camp (steppe ordu)
nomad-camp.description: A steppe nomad camp (ordu): felt gers (yurts) in a radial circle around a central tent.

swahili-stone-town.label: Swahili stone town (Lamu / Zanzibar)
swahili-stone-town.description: A Swahili stone town (Lamu, Zanzibar): flat-roofed coral-stone houses of two to three storeys on organic lanes, a mosque at the centre.

drow-enclave.label: Drow enclave
drow-enclave.description: A drow enclave: dark-stone courtyard houses of two to three storeys with flat roofs, on organic lanes around a central precinct.

duergar-hold.label: Duergar industrial hold
duergar-hold.description: A duergar industrial hold: terraced dark-stone halls with flat roofs, behind a straight wall, around a central precinct.

myconid-colony.label: Myconid colony
myconid-colony.description: A myconid colony: domed fungal dwellings in a radial plan around a central precinct, no wall.

egyptian-planned.label: Egypt: planned Nile city
egyptian-planned.description: Compact rectilinear quarters oriented on the valley; sacred complexes remain reserves, with no temple generation.

nubian-fortified.label: Nubia: fortified town
nubian-fortified.description: Brick blocks within a compact wall, tied to the banks of the Nile.

mesopotamian.label: Mesopotamia: courtyard quarters
mesopotamian.description: Massive courtyard blocks, market streets and alleys; canals and temples are not synthesised by this recipe.

levantine-tell.label: Levant: fortified tell town
levantine-tell.description: Slope streets and walls adapted to the relief; the existing tell belongs to the scenery.

oasis-caravan.label: Central Asia: oasis caravan city
oasis-caravan.description: Caravan axes between gates, a market core and large enclosures; irrigation and citadel remain future reserves.

ksar-oasis.label: Maghreb: oasis ksar
ksar-oasis.description: A very compact core with defensive approaches and alleys; distinct from the kasbah and from the urban medina.

yoruba.label: Yoruba: compound city
yoruba.description: Large lineage enclosures, quarters and market axes; no copy of the late palaces of Abomey.

himalayan-terraces.label: Tibet and Ladakh: terraced settlement
himalayan-terraces.description: Alleys following the contours, compact blocks and stairs; no automatic late dzong.

newar.label: Newar Nepal: city of ritual squares
newar.description: Dense blocks around courtyards and ritual squares; palace pavilions are not generated here.

indus-planned.label: Indus: Harappan city
indus-planned.description: A hierarchical grid, blocks of courtyard houses and lanes; drainage networks are not yet produced.

javanese-courts.label: Java: city of courts and enclosures
javanese-courts.description: Large enclosures, public squares and separate courts; this recipe does not confuse Java with the temples of India.

mississippian.label: Mississippian: centre with a palisaded plaza
mississippian.description: An open plaza, paths and large blocks of houses and gardens; artificial mounds are still to be integrated with the relief.

al-andalus.label: Al-Andalus: Iberian medina with courtyards
al-andalus.description: A souk and great mosque at the centre, courtyard houses served by dead-end adarves, arrabales outside the walls and landscaped cármenes at the edge.

italian-comune.label: Italy: commune with piazza and towers
italian-comune.description: A civic piazza at the heart, successive rings of walls (cerchie), massive blocks of narrow arcaded houses; borghi along the roads outside the gates.

flemish-cloth-town.label: Flanders: cloth town with a belfry
flemish-cloth-town.description: A Grand-Place and the belfry of the cloth hall, canals (reien) and successive walls; gabled street houses and deep plots for dyers and fullers.

rynek-town.label: Central Europe: rynek town
rynek-town.description: A founded town (Magdeburg law): a large square market with a hall and town hall, a checkerboard of streets, deep burgher plots; suburbs along the roads.

slavic-gord.label: Slavs: palisaded gord and podgrodzie
slavic-gord.description: A wood-and-earth gord on the height, a craft podgrodzie at its foot, streets paved with logs and large courtyards of log houses.

caucasian-highland.label: Caucasus: Georgian and Armenian fortified town
caucasian-highland.description: A church in a fortified enclosure at the summit, tight stone houses in terraces, alleys and stairs following the contours.

ethiopian-highland.label: Ethiopia: highland city (Aksum, Lalibela)
ethiopian-highland.description: A circular church enclosure on the height, family compounds of round houses surrounded by hedges, curving paths; stelae and rock-hewn churches remain reserves.

great-zimbabwe.label: Zimbabwe: dry-stone enclosure
great-zimbabwe.description: A great royal dry-stone enclosure at the centre, compounds of daga huts ringed by curving low walls, settlement loosening towards the valley.

hausa-kano.label: Hausa: city-state within an earth wall (Kano)
hausa-kano.description: A great mosque, the emir’s palace and the Kurmi market at the centre; courtyard compounds behind a vestibule (zaure), dead-end alleys, a vast earth wall enclosing fields and ponds.

hadhrami-tower.label: Hadhramaut: vertical city of tower houses (Shibam)
hadhrami-tower.description: A compact rectangular wall on a mound in the valley, tower houses of five to eight storeys almost touching, small squares and alleys; palm groves outside the walls.

rajput-fort.label: Rajputana: city below the fort (Jaisalmer, Amber)
rajput-fort.description: A royal fort on the spur, a bazaar between the gates, courtyard havelis in narrow alleys; a pond (talab) and stepwells as service reserves.

dravidian-temple.label: South India: temple city with concentric streets (Madurai)
dravidian-temple.description: The temple enclosure and its gopurams at the centre, concentric square processional streets (masi, avani, chitrai), rows of narrow deep houses; a sacred tank.

bagan.label: Burma: royal city of Pagan
bagan.description: A square walled city with the palace on the riverbank, stilt houses in large planted enclosures, monasteries and stupas scattered over the plain.

vietnamese-citadel.label: Vietnam: citadel and merchant quarter (Thăng Long)
vietnamese-citadel.description: A square moated citadel with cardinal gates, courtyard houses in enclosures; outside the walls, the merchant quarter of the “36 streets” with narrow deep tube houses.

tibetan-monastery.label: Tibet: monastic town on a slope
tibetan-monastery.description: A monastery and assembly hall at the top of the slope, cells and flat-roofed houses stepping down, a pilgrimage circuit (kora) around; no automatic dzong.

mongol-ordu.label: Mongols: ordu, a princely camp of yurts
mongol-ordu.description: The khan’s tent at the centre, open to the south, rings and rows of clan yurts, wide lanes for wagons; beyond a threshold, a fixed walled capital on a checkerboard (Karakorum).

maori-pa.label: Māori: terraced fortified pā
maori-pa.description: A hill or spur cut into terraces defended by ditches and palisades, a marae and meeting house on the high platform, whare and pataka packed on the steps.

pnw-plank-village.label: Northwest Coast: plank-house village
pnw-plank-village.description: A row of large cedar-plank clan houses, painted fronts and poles facing the beach, canoes and drying racks on the shore.

inuit-camp.label: Arctic: Inuit winter camp
inuit-camp.description: A group of igloos and skin tents near the shore or the pack ice, a communal house (qaggiq) at the centre, caches and drying racks around.

siberian-camp.label: Siberia: reindeer herders’ chum camp
siberian-camp.description: Conical tents in an open arc, sledges and caches on posts behind, reindeer pens at the edge; a log village from a few hundred inhabitants.

guarani-village.label: Guaraní: village of great houses (tekoha)
guarani-village.description: A few large communal houses (óga guasu) around a dance plaza, a palisade and a ring of manioc and maize clearings.

budj-bim.label: Australia: Budj Bim stone village
budj-bim.description: Dry-stone huts grouped on the lava flows near eel channels and traps; the dams remain scenery.

lizardfolk-swamp.label: Lizardfolk: lake city on stilts
lizardfolk-swamp.description: The morphology of pile-dwelling villages: platforms on stilts linked by winding walkways around a sacred pool; no wide streets.

merfolk-tidal.label: Merfolk: tidal village of shore and sea caves
merfolk-tidal.description: The morphology of lagoons and islets (Nan Madol, pile villages): houses on platforms at water level, stair-alleys to the caves, a tidal shrine at the centre.

giant-hold.label: Giants: megalithic town
giant-hold.description: The morphology of a ring fort at ×2–3 scale: the jarl’s great hall at the centre, oversized streets and enclosures, a cyclopean wall; the houses remain human recipes (a known gap).

goblin-warren.label: Goblins: hillside warren
goblin-warren.description: The morphology of semi-subterranean house villages: mounds dug out in clusters, highly branched dead-end tunnels following the slope, a stake palisade; no ordered square.

american-grid.label: American grid city (Chicago, Manhattan)
american-grid.description: Orthogonal grid of long rectangular blocks between avenues and cross streets; brick and stone row houses and walk-up tenements on narrow deep lots; a vertical business core of commercial blocks and setback towers; station, factories, warehouses and elevators near the water. No town wall.

industrial-victorian.label: Industrial Victorian city (Manchester, Liverpool)
industrial-victorian.description: Brick terraces and back-to-back rows on a tight grid of narrow streets; mills with their chimneys, warehouses, canals and railway yards; a civic core of town hall, exchange and covered market. No town wall.

haussmannian.label: Haussmannian boulevard city (Paris)
haussmannian.description: Straight boulevards and radiating avenues cut through closed blocks; continuous stone apartment fronts of equal height under zinc mansards; squares at the crossings, a station, an opera and a great department store.

belle-epoque.label: Belle Époque capital (Vienna, Budapest)
belle-epoque.description: A ring boulevard around the old core lined with monumental public buildings; large courtyard blocks of bourgeois apartment houses with hipped roofs; tram avenues, parks and a grand station.

mediterranean-modern.label: Mediterranean modern city (Barcelona, Naples)
mediterranean-modern.description: A regular grid of chamfered square blocks with inner patios; party-wall apartment buildings with balconies and roof terraces; a seafront promenade, a port and a market hall.

garden-city.label: Garden city (Letchworth, Welwyn)
garden-city.description: Curving tree-lined streets and closes around greens; semi-detached cottages and short terraces in deep gardens; a civic centre, a parkway and a separate industrial estate.

art-deco-metropolis.label: Art Deco metropolis (New York, Miami)
art-deco-metropolis.description: A dense grid of avenues and streets under setback towers crowned by stepped spires; geometric stone and brick apartment blocks, hotels and theatres along the grand axes.

modernist-functionalist.label: Modernist functional city (Brasília, Chandigarh)
modernist-functionalist.description: Superblocks between wide arterial roads without crossings; free-standing slabs on pilotis in open lawns; separate zones for housing, government, commerce and industry; a monumental axis with the stadium and the towers of administration.

soviet-socialist.label: Soviet socialist city (Moscow, Minsk)
soviet-socialist.description: Wide parade avenues and a central square with its monument; microdistricts of prefabricated panel slabs around schools and courtyards; Stalinist towers, a television tower, power plants and factory belts.

american-suburbia.label: American suburbia (Los Angeles, Phoenix)
american-suburbia.description: Curving residential loops and cul-de-sacs off a hierarchy of arterials; detached houses with garages on deep front lawns; shopping malls, strip centres and office parks at the interchanges.

european-contemporary.label: European contemporary city (Copenhagen, Amsterdam)
european-contemporary.description: Mixed perimeter blocks around green courts; brick and timber apartment buildings over shops; canals, tram and cycle streets, a central station and a harbour front of cultural buildings.

global-high-rise.label: Global high-rise city (Hong Kong, Shenzhen)
global-high-rise.description: Residential towers on commercial podiums packed between steep slopes and the harbour; elevated walkways, metro stations and malls; a skyline of glass office towers.

gulf-contemporary.label: Gulf city (Dubai, Doha)
gulf-contemporary.description: Discontinuous growth along wide motorways; walled villa superblocks; a strip of iconic towers along the coast; air-conditioned malls, a grand mosque and marinas.

informal-urban-expansion.label: Informal urban expansion (Lagos, Lima)
informal-urban-expansion.description: Self-built houses on irregular plots along narrow lanes, extended storey by storey; corrugated roofs, open markets, churches and mosques, workshops in every street.

eco-city.label: Eco-city (sustainable district)
eco-city.description: Low-carbon timber blocks with green roofs around green corridors; car-free streets, cycle and tram lines, community gardens, greenhouses and a wind-powered utility edge.

japanese-contemporary.label: Japanese contemporary city (Tokyo, Osaka)
japanese-contemporary.description: Tiny plots on narrow local streets behind wide arterials; pencil buildings, detached houses with small gaps between them, shops on every corner; elevated railways, stations with their department stores and temple and shrine precincts.

chinese-megacity.label: Chinese megacity (Shanghai, Guangzhou)
chinese-megacity.description: Gated superblocks of identical residential towers between eight-lane avenues; a CBD of glass skyscrapers, malls and elevated ring roads; old lane quarters and villages swallowed by the grid.

korean-high-rise.label: Korean high-rise city (Seoul, Busan)
korean-high-rise.description: Numbered apartment estates (danji) of parallel high-rise slabs climbing the hills; dense low-rise villa quarters and markets between them; churches with neon crosses and a mountain backdrop.

southeast-asian-tropical.label: Southeast Asian tropical city (Bangkok, Ho Chi Minh City)
southeast-asian-tropical.description: Narrow shophouse rows along main roads with deep alleys (soi) behind them; markets, canals and temples; a few towers and malls on the arterials.

south-asian-metropolis.label: South Asian metropolis (Mumbai, Delhi)
south-asian-metropolis.description: Extreme density of mixed blocks: chawls, apartment buildings and self-built quarters side by side; bazaars, temples, a colonial railway terminus and planned colonies at the edge.

latin-american-grid.label: Latin American grid city (Buenos Aires, Mexico City)
latin-american-grid.description: The colonial grid of square blocks around the plaza mayor; patio houses and apartment buildings on compact lots; wide avenues and diagonals of the nineteenth century, a cathedral, a cabildo and a station.

latin-american-hillside.label: Latin American hillside city (Rio, Medellín)
latin-american-hillside.description: Brick houses clinging to steep slopes, stacked along stairs and winding lanes; a dense irregular network climbing from the valley road, cable-car stations, chapels and football pitches.

north-african-contemporary.label: North African contemporary city (Casablanca, Tunis)
north-african-contemporary.description: A colonial ville nouvelle of white Art Deco apartment buildings on boulevards beside the old medina; modern housing estates and self-built peripheries; a grand mosque, souks and a port.

sub-saharan-african-metropolis.label: Sub-Saharan African metropolis (Dakar, Accra)
sub-saharan-african-metropolis.description: A colonial plateau of offices and avenues above heterogeneous quarters of walled family compounds, densifying year by year; great markets, mosques and churches, bus stations.

middle-eastern-contemporary.label: Middle Eastern contemporary city (Amman, Beirut)
middle-eastern-contemporary.description: Free-standing stone-clad apartment blocks with roof terraces on stepped hillside streets; a dense old centre of souks, mosques and churches; circles and boulevards on the ridges.

australian-suburban.label: Australian suburban city (Perth, Brisbane)
australian-suburban.description: Low-density suburbs of single-storey houses under metal roofs on quarter-acre blocks; wide roads, shopping centres and a compact CBD of towers on the river.

post-socialist-european.label: Post-socialist European city (Warsaw, Bucharest)
post-socialist-european.description: A rebuilt historic core ringed by vast estates of panel blocks; a Stalinist palace of culture, new glass office towers, malls and car dealerships along the exit roads.

cyberpunk.label: Cyberpunk megacity
cyberpunk.description: Extreme vertical density: corporate megatowers and arcologies over stacked housing slabs, elevated decks and multi-level streets; markets in the undercity, power plants and data towers.

solarpunk.label: Solarpunk garden city
solarpunk.description: Planted terraces and green roofs over timber blocks along curving car-free streets; vertical farms, greenhouses, solar fields and wind masts; parks and water gardens everywhere.

dieselpunk.label: Dieselpunk industrial metropolis
dieselpunk.description: Monumental Art Deco towers, smokestacks and steel works on heroic avenues; worker blocks in brick, power stations, airship mooring masts and rail yards.

dystopian-brutalism.label: Dystopian brutalist city
dystopian-brutalism.description: Massive raw-concrete blocks repeated along an authoritarian axis; megastructures, ministries and monuments; vast empty squares, cooling towers and walled industrial zones.

atompunk-retrofuturist.label: Atompunk retrofuturist city
atompunk-retrofuturist.description: The future as imagined around 1960: ring roads and space-age houses under flat and domed roofs; streamlined towers, saucer pavilions under domes, broadcasting masts and an atomic power plant.

post-apocalyptic-ruins.label: Post-apocalyptic ruins
post-apocalyptic-ruins.description: An abandoned modern grid: ruined blocks and dead towers reclaimed by vegetation, among them rebuilt salvage houses, scrap markets and fortified compounds.

corporate-arcology.label: Corporate arcology
corporate-arcology.description: One integrated megastructure holds the city: a stepped arcology at the centre, ring roads and terraced blocks around it, private plazas, transit and power in the outer ring.

futuristic-space-colony.label: Space colony
futuristic-space-colony.description: Pressurised domes and modular habitats on a radial plan of corridors; a great central dome, landing pads, power plants and hydroponic greenhouses.

biopunk-organic-city.label: Biopunk organic city
biopunk-organic-city.description: Living structures grown rather than built: biomorphic pods and towers along branching, curving paths; a central hive, organic spires and spawning gardens.
